name: Freezing Cold
description: A freezing face with an ice cube means the sender is physically cold, or dramatically claiming to be. It is weather and body temperature. It is a bad way to call someone cruel.
meaning: The cold face is the feeling and the ice is the proof, or the joke that even the ice agrees. 🥶🧊 means "I am freezing." The slang "ice cold" for a harsh person is too ambiguous here. They will think you mean the thermostat.
seoDescription: What does 🥶🧊 mean? The sender is freezing. It is cold weather or a cold room, not a clean way to call someone harsh.

longForm.overview:
The cold face is already a full performance: blue cheeks, teeth you can imagine chattering, a person insisting the temperature is a personal attack. An ice cube next to it removes the remaining doubt about mood versus weather. 🥶🧊 is cold you could slip on. People send it from bus stops, bad offices, first swims of the season, and apartments where the heat has not come on. They want sympathy, a joke, or permission to come inside. They rarely want a debate about whether the cold is objectively severe. The performance is the message. You can grant it.

There is a slang trap. "Ice cold" describes a person who was harsh, stylishly detached, or cruel. This pair is a clumsy way to say that, because both glyphs are literal temperature to most readers. "That text was 🥶🧊" might mean the message was brutal, and it might mean the sender's hands were cold while they typed. If you mean cruel, use words. If you mean winter, the pair is perfect and a little whiny, which is part of its charm. Do not send it to mock someone who is actually suffering in the cold without shelter. A cute ice cube is not a response to that. Offer help or say nothing theatrical.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🥶🧊 is a small-talk engine in winter group chats and a real complaint in households. Roommates send it hoping someone else will check the thermostat. Parents send it to kids who left in a jacket that was a suggestion. Photos of frost and sad indoor picnics get the pair as a caption.

It also marks dramatic people at mild temperatures. If you know your friend calls 60 degrees arctic, you can tease them. If you do not know, assume they are actually uncomfortable.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Do not use 🥶🧊 as an insult about someone's personality. The literal reading will win, and if the insult reading wins, you called them cruel with a joke you can pretend was weather. That is a messy way to be unkind.

Do not send it as the only content of a safety issue. A car broken down in a storm needs a location and a request, not a cube. And skip the bit in a professional email about a freezer malfunction unless your team already talks this way. Say the freezer failed.
longForm.howToReply:
Offer the practical thing if you have it: a ride, a blanket, a "the heat is on now." Matching the pair is enough when you are suffering in the same room.

If you think they mean someone was harsh, ask. "Weather or that message?" takes one line and prevents you from consoling a thermostat. If they are teasing you for being cold-natured, you can defend your jacket and move on.

faqs.question: What does 🥶🧊 mean?
faqs.answer: 🥶🧊 means the sender is freezing. The cold face is the feeling. The ice cube insists the cold is literal.

faqs.question: Does 🥶🧊 mean someone was mean?
faqs.answer: It might be an attempt at "ice cold," but most people will read temperature. If you mean a cruel message, say cruel. Do not rely on the cube.

faqs.question: What does 🥶🧊 mean in a house chat?
faqs.answer: Usually that a room is too cold and they want the heat adjusted, or they want to complain about it together.

faqs.question: How do I reply to 🥶🧊?
faqs.answer: Sympathize or offer something warm. A practical fix beats a second ice cube when they are actually stuck outside.

conversationExamples.interpretation: They are cold and joking about the plan. Suggest moving inside. Do not extend the outdoor reservation.
A household problem, not only a mood. Ask if they need a repair call or a place to go.

conversationExamples.message: the office AC is 🥶🧊 bring a layer
conversationExamples.interpretation: A practical warning to coworkers. Bring the layer. They are not describing a person.

conversationExamples.message: I will look cute and also 🥶🧊, fair warning
conversationExamples.interpretation: They are dressing for a look, not the weather. Offer a jacket without turning it into a lecture.

conversationExamples.message: game is outside and I am 🥶🧊 in the stands
conversationExamples.interpretation: A live complaint from an event. Commiserate. They may not answer until halftime.
